plan_a_advantages: Lower overall volume (fewer minutes of training) which might be suitable for a beginner or someone recovering from injury.
Simpler structure, potentially easier to adhere to for some individuals.
plan_b_advantages: Includes hill and threshold work, directly addressing the demands of trail running.
Longer, more focused aerobic session builds greater endurance.
More varied workout types promote a more holistic training approach.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted training stimuli, specifically hill work and threshold intervals, which are crucial for developing the power and strength needed for trail running. Plan A, while providing a solid base with easy runs, lacks this focused intensity and neglects key elements of trail-specific fitness. Furthermore, the longer, consistent easy runs in Plan B contribute to greater aerobic endurance, a critical component for sustained performance on trails. Plan A’s emphasis on simply completing easy runs risks becoming monotonous and failing to adequately challenge the athlete.
